editorial.headline: Sugarcane Farming With a Clear Bali Path
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 01140 covers integrated sugarcane cultivation, from land preparation through harvest and post-harvest work, and remains open nationally and in Bali for PMA registration.
editorial.body:
KBLI 01140 is the activity code for sugarcane farming as a complete agricultural operation. Its scope is practical and field-based: preparing the land, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting it, and handling post-harvest work when those steps are carried out as one chain of sugarcane cultivation. It also includes sugarcane nursery and seedling activities, as well as land processing, sowing, planting, crop care, and harvest when they form a single sugarcane farming activity.

The code is therefore best understood as cultivation, not merely a trading label or an isolated service around the crop. A founder using it should be registering a business whose real activity is the growing of sugarcane, including the agronomic steps that make the crop possible. The record is broad enough to cover both the farming cycle itself and the propagation work that supports it, but its centre remains the same: organised sugarcane agriculture.

On scale, the code is open across the full range recorded here: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That matters because the activity is not confined to smallholder registration or reserved only for larger operators. The record supports registration from micro-scale operations through large-scale businesses. For foreign investment, the national position is also straightforward: PMA status is TERBUKA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100% under the stated PMA source.

The Bali picture is unusually clean compared with activities that are caught by the province’s moratorium. The record says Bali blocks all low and medium-low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently, but this code is not blocked because OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. In plain terms, the honest reading is that a foreign investor can register this sugarcane farming activity in Bali today, subject to the recorded national openness and the risk-status basis stated in the slim record. The important nuance is not a hidden restriction; it is the reason the Bali moratorium does not stop this code.
